name: HARDEN
label: Month 4 · Eval infrastructure + START APPLYING
goal: Turn evals into CI. Then open the job search while you keep building.

weeks.title: Re-entry (deliberately light)
weeks.why: Coming back from three weeks off, the failure mode is starting new material immediately, getting confused, and concluding you have lost it. You have not. This week is intentionally under-loaded: reload context, ship one small thing, rebuild momentum.

tasks.t: Read your own Week 9 handover note and all your site notes from Months 1-2
Re-run the full eval harness. Fix whatever broke (dependency drift, expired keys, model deprecations).
Re-explain the tool loop to yourself from memory, out loud. Check against your Week 4 code.
Ship ONE small improvement to the RAG pipeline and measure it. Any improvement. The point is a green delta.
Re-plan: look at the remaining weeks and adjust anything that no longer fits your life

weeks.deliverable: A working stack, one measured improvement, and your head back in the game.
weeks.checkpoint: Do you still believe you can do this? If yes, the pause cost you three weeks and nothing else.

weeks.title: Evals as infrastructure, not a script
weeks.why: A notebook that computes recall is a homework exercise. A CI job that blocks a merge when recall drops is engineering. This distinction is what makes an 'AI Engineer' rather than someone who did an LLM course.

tasks.t: Convert eval.py into a pytest suite with real assertions and thresholds
Run it in GitHub Actions on every PR. Free for public repos.
Regression gates: fail the build if recall@5 drops more than 2 points from the committed baseline
Version your golden set. Treat it like a schema migration — when it changes, say why in the commit.
Try promptfoo — declarative prompt/model comparison, open source, no signup
Cache eval runs so CI does not cost you money on every push (and so you can afford to run it often)
AT WORK: pitch one AI feature to your manager, using the workflow list from Week 0. Ask for 3 hours a week.

resources.label: promptfoo — open-source prompt/RAG evaluation and red-teaming
Hamel Husain — creating a LLM-as-a-judge that drives business results

weeks.deliverable: A CI pipeline that runs your evals on every PR and blocks regressions. Screenshot the failing build — it is interview material.
weeks.checkpoint: Open a PR that makes retrieval worse. Does CI catch it?

weeks.title: Observability and cost per request
weeks.why: 'What does one request cost you?' is a standard interview question and most candidates have no answer. Having a number — and knowing which component dominates it — puts you immediately above the pile.

tasks.t: Structured logging with a trace id threaded through the whole request
Instrument spans: retrieval / rerank / generation. Find out where the time actually goes (it is rarely where you think).
Token accounting per request: input, output, cached. Compute cost per request and per user session.
p50 / p95 / p99 latency. Know why p95 matters and averages lie.
Build a small dashboard (Langfuse UI, or your own FastAPI + a chart) showing cost and latency over time
Error taxonomy in prod: rate limits, timeouts, refusals, malformed structured output. Count each.

resources.label: OpenTelemetry for LLM apps — semantic conventions for GenAI
Chip Huyen — building LLM applications for production

weeks.deliverable: A dashboard showing cost per request and p95 latency broken down by pipeline stage.
weeks.checkpoint: What is your cost per request, and which stage dominates it? Answer in one sentence with a number.

weeks.title: OPEN THE JOB SEARCH
weeks.why: This is where I diverge hardest from the original plan. You are 16 weeks in with a measured RAG system, a CI eval harness, and a cost dashboard — that is already an interviewable profile. Hiring cycles run 6-10 weeks. Start now and offers land while you finish Months 5-7 instead of three months after.

tasks.t: Rewrite your resume around METRICS. Every bullet: what you built, what it measured, what changed. Delete every bullet without a number.
Rewrite LinkedIn headline and About. Target: 'AI Engineer' keywords — RAG, evals, LLM, FastAPI, agents, vector search.
Write the README for the RAG project as if a hiring manager is the only reader. Before/after table above the fold.
Build a target list of 40 companies: product cos, funded startups, GCCs. Explicitly EXCLUDE service companies — they will anchor you at 7-9 LPA.
Send the first 20 applications. Prioritise referrals — cold applications convert at ~2%, referrals at ~20%.

ARCHITECTURE WALKTHROUGH: draw ONE diagram of your RAG system, list the 5 tradeoffs you made and why, rehearse it out loud. At 2 YOE this IS the system design round — it just arrives disguised as 'walk me through your project'.
Do one mock interview (Pramp / a friend / record yourself). Expect it to go badly. That is the entire point of doing it now.
Write your 3-minute project pitch and rehearse it out loud until it is boring to you

resources.label: Anthropic — interviewing tips (applies broadly to AI eng roles)
Pramp / Exponent free mock interview matching
levels.fyi India — calibrate your salary ask with data

weeks.deliverable: 20 applications sent, a metrics-driven resume, and one embarrassing mock interview behind you.
weeks.checkpoint: Does your resume contain at least three numbers? If not, rewrite it.
